audit_correction.reason: The original audit compared the pinned library source inventory to an inventory with two new Python observation scripts. The successor checks all 574 original files unchanged and permits exactly the two declared scripts; no Rust rebuild or GPU rerun is needed.

limitations: Observation starts before coordinator launch and captures pre-READY through both jobs to pidfd exit, but polling misses the first few milliseconds and may miss transient peaks.
RSS, PSS, virtual mapping size, and cgroup charged memory have different meanings. Independently sampled maxima cannot be added or treated as identical.
Mapping names classify backing, not allocation ownership. Anonymous mappings may include thread stacks and runtime/driver storage; the labeled stack is not every thread stack.
Twelve observed threads and the observed resident peaks are not worst-case upper bounds.
Sampler overhead makes these proof timings unsuitable for throughput comparisons.
Allocator/runtime/stacks, driver/shared-engine ownership and other caller backing still need complete overlapping-phase RSS accounting. Ordinary workload admission remains closed.
Broader/live-cache workloads, five alternating matched throughput pairs, 24 hours AND 150 roots, full-64/deadline/depth/size gates, multiple GPUs, AMD/Metal and Apple source integration remain open.
next_work: Derive and enforce runtime/thread/allocator and shared driver ownership limits rather than substituting observed peaks for bounds.
Compose those host allowances with caller, protocol, typed-input, witness/compiler and PCS lifetimes before admitting ordinary pool workloads.
Validate the resulting admission model against startup, warm reuse, simultaneous cache ownership, faults/cancellation and teardown on each supported backend.
